location: Fictional California college campus and the streets around it (G4m p001 calls it a corner of the "California College campus"; the PS1 bowl floor is painted "California College", VG)
timeLimit: original: none (free roam, each goal has its own clock, usually 2:00); remake: 10:00 run
versions: PS2 2002 (Neversoft) — goal list and routes from G4m, THG and LP4
PS1 2002 (Vicarious Visions port) — VG maps and CC1 text
THPS 3+4 2025 (Iron Galaxy remake) — PS34, LP34 and WEB
sources: WEB pcgamesn, gamerant (college tape; college goals), screenrant, thegamer, operationsports

goals.text: Collect the C-O-M-B-O letters (all in one combo, from Ollie the Bum)
Nail the tricks they yell out
Get back at the 5 frat boys
Stop all of the Pink Elephants
Combo the benches, stairs and flagpole (50,000)
Tony Hawk's pro challenge (roof halfpipe gap transfers)
Jamie Thomas's pro challenge (a day-in-the-life trick line)
Boneless Spine Transfer Between the Courts

size.footprint: ≈ 300-400 m × 250-300 m including the outer streets and the hill
size.evidence: G4m p013-p014 top-down map scaled by its two tennis courts taken as regulation 23.8 m long (146 px on the page, so ≈ 0.16 m/px); game courts may be smaller than regulation, so treat as an upper bound; low confidence

zones.name: West street and Woodland School
zones.layer: ground street; school steps and handrail; awnings

shops along the outer side (Billy's Sporting Goods, Schnitzel World further south)
zones.notes: Outer ring road that wraps the campus on the west and south; the school roof carries a halfpipe reached by the "Class Transfer" (G4m p007). Remake keeps the Woodland School facade (LP34 1:06:45 flythrough).

red rail and raised barrier gate at the garage corner
power lines strung over the road (High Road Hop to the K)
the Professor's car on the second level (remake)
zones.notes: Highest street-side structure; its barrier gate is the stepping stone from ground to the wire layer. Skate Rat stands on this corner (G4m p013-p014).

zones.name: South street: frat house, garbage truck, campus wall
zones.layer: ground; awnings and balconies (≈ 3-6 m); top of the campus wall (≈ 3-4 m)

garbage truck parked outside the frat house (spine transfer into it for the A; Garbage Day side job)
large beige campus wall with blue arches carrying 7 election banners
parade floats circulating on the road (pro goal)
shipping containers with a quarter pipe (remake)
zones.notes: The campus wall is a long grindable ledge reached only by wallride or wallie: the level's first lesson in leaving the ground without a ramp.

spawn.zone: Z1 (original) / Z1-Z3 outer road at the campus edge (remake)
spawn.facing: Original: on the outer-road sidewalk facing up the street toward a green steel arch that spans the road, clock tower above the roofs beyond (LP4 0:05:26). Remake: beside the outer road; banner wall to the right, clock tower ahead along the axis (PS34; WEB gamerant).
visibleCollectibles: no letter confirmed visible from spawn
spawn.notes: LP4 0:05:26-0:05:30: first frame of play shows the skater on the sidewalk of the outer road, a tutorial box about talking to people with arrows over their heads, a green steel arch spanning the street ahead and the clock tower above the roofs; at 0:05:36 a Skate Rat with a blue arrow stands by the shops. LP34 1:07:10: run starts on a curving concrete walk with grass; 1:07:15 is already at the tennis courts. PS34 directions ("from level start go left down the street", "turn right and spine transfer into the shipping containers", "look to the right and wallride up to grind the first banner") place the remake start beside the outer road and the banner wall.

collectibles.label: Secret tape (remake)
collectibles.landmark: wire from the clock-tower top down to the flat roof of a three-storey brick building beside the bowl
collectibles.heightM: ≈ 12-16 m above the plaza; ≈ 2-4 m above the brick roof at the wire's lower end (estimated from LP34 1:10:03-1:10:04: three rows of windows ≈ 10 m against a 1.8 m skater)
collectibles.launchFrom: the clock-tower portal (door at the back of the tower base) drops the skater on the wire at the top

visibility.firstSight: level-start goal flythrough shows the tape beside the brick building corner with a pennant string (LP34 1:07:05); the tower is visible down the street axis (LP34 1:09:46) and from the plaza (PS34 screenshot)
visibility.reads: small glowing cassette icon on a thin black wire high above the campus; the wire itself reads against the sky
visibility.distanceFromFirstSightM: ≈ 30-60 from the tower terrace (route length), but the tape is first identifiable only from the wire or the flythrough

route.from: outer street below the campus gate
route.geometry: Ride up the outer street toward the gate; the clock tower stands at the end of the axis (LP34 1:09:46-1:09:49).
Cross the plaza and its fountain ring (LP34 1:09:50-1:09:54).
Grind the curved handrail up the steps toward the tower (LP34 1:09:55-1:09:57).
Ride or grind the terrace ledge round to the rear of the tower (LP34 1:09:58-1:09:59).

route.from: open green double door with a small wooden kicker at its threshold
route.geometry: Roll through the door: a portal relocates the skater to the top of the tower and launches him onto the wire (LP34 1:10:00-1:10:01; PS34 screenshot of the door).
Hold a 50-50 down the long descending wire; the tape registers as the wire nears the brick building (LP34 1:10:02-1:10:04, "COMPLETE! Get the secret tape" at 7:19).
Land on the brick building's flat roof (LP34 1:10:05) and drop back to the plaza.

skillGates: wire balance on a long descending grind
knowing the tower door is a portal (not signposted in text; the open door and kicker are the cue)
collectibles.coupling: portal door at the tower base; no goal unlock needed (used in the first run of LP34; PS34 lists no prerequisite)
collectibles.failure: Falling off the wire drops 10-20 m onto the bowl/plaza area; a bail costs a few seconds and the door is ≈ 10 s away, so retries are cheap inside a 10:00 run.
collectibles.timeFromSpawnS: ≈ 18 s from the street below the gate, ≈ 4 s from the door (LP34 1:09:46 → 1:10:04); the run had started 2:54 earlier (1:07:10) because the player did other goals first
collectibles.why: The level's tallest landmark is the tape's home: the tower is seen from the street and the plaza, the flythrough shows the tape, and the player only has to ask "what is behind the tower?". The portal turns a 25 m climb into a free ride and rewards the climb with the best view of the campus; a harder uphill approach exists for players who arrive by the rooftop wires.
collectibles.evidence: PS34 college "Get the Secret Tape"; WEB pcgamesn, thegamer, operationsports, screenrant, gamerant; LP34 1:07:05, 1:09:46-1:10:05; PS34 screenshots 31-33

altRoutes.name: uphill rooftop chain (hard)
altRoutes.evidence: WEB gamerant college tape guide; WEB screenrant

route.geometry: Wallride the wall before the first pillar and grind its top for about a second.
Jump right into a grind on the bunting string over the street.
Halfway along, hop left onto a black wire and grind up to a rooftop; trick during the grind to keep speed and jump off before the wire ends.
Grind the right-hand lip of the rooftop halfpipes; the grind continues onto a second wire across the campus.
Jump left, turn sharply and drop onto the brick building (a gap in its roof punishes an over-turn).
Start a grind on the roof's left edge, which links into the steep, long uphill wire; flip and grab while grinding to keep momentum until the tape.

guidance: Clock tower as beacon: visible from the original spawn (LP4 0:05:30) and as the end point of the remake street axis (LP34 1:09:46); the tape is on its wire.
Goal flythrough (remake): each run starts by showing every goal location, including the tape beside the brick building (LP34 1:06:45-1:07:05); WEB gamerant notes the flythrough hints every tape.
Open door with a kicker at the back of the tower base is the only cue to the portal (PS34 screenshot); it is out of sight from the front, so finding it is exploration.
Arrows over goal givers' heads and the tutorial text direct the original player to people, not places (LP4 0:05:30).
Bunting and pennant strings strung between buildings read as grindable wires in the remake (PS34 screenshot 31; WEB gamerant).
Letters ride on obvious launchers: S over the door at the end of a handrail, T over a QP, A over a truck, K on a power line above a sloped gate arm (G4m p003).
Election banners and graffiti mark the long wall as a grind surface (G4m p011; LP34 1:07:00 "VOTE DICK" flythrough).
Hidden on purpose: the tower portal, Central Hall's second storey (PS1), the remake elevator to a rooftop, and the rooftop wire network.
designLogic: The tape uses the level's tallest and most visible landmark; the challenge is not seeing it but finding the way up (EXPLORE), and the portal makes the way up a secret rather than a feat (remake TAPE-R; PS1 Clock Tower gap).

A tower-top wire exists in all three versions (PS2 gap "Clock tower Grind", PS1 "High Wire Act" 200 from the tower top to Central Hall and "Clock Tower" 350 for the portal, remake tape wire). Inferred: Iron Galaxy put the tape on a line the 2002 versions already rewarded with gaps, so the tape points players at an old secret.

Two approaches to one tape: a fast secret (door, downhill wire, ≈ 4 s) and a skilled public route (rooftop wire chain, uphill, tricks to keep speed). The collectible rewards either knowledge or execution.

Wire placement escalates: K on a power line reached from a gate arm (one hop from the ground), then remake car-park wires, then roof-to-roof wires, then the tower wire. Each wire collectible starts higher than the last.

Original letters are a guided tour: the S-K-A-T-E order runs from the outer street (S, K, A) into the campus (T, E) and each letter adds one verb (grind, wire, spine transfer, vert air, air-to-grind).
THPS4 hides nothing until a goal is accepted: letters and goal objects only appear after talking to a giver, so the original's "hard-to-reach" layer lives in gaps and pro goals, not in tapes.
Free roam removes the 2-minute pressure from exploration but each goal still has a clock (S-K-A-T-E 2:00; record 56.37 s), so letter routes stay short and local even in a 300 m map.
Buildings are permeable: frat windows (three named gaps), Central Hall's second storey (PS1), the tower portal and the remake elevator all turn walls into routes and give secret-area rewards.
Long boundary walls become grind lines through goals (banners on the campus wall; frat boys on the wall top), which teaches wallride and wallie as entry moves before the rooftop routes need them.
Failure is cheap near the ground (letters over QPs, rails a few metres up) and only expensive on the wire layer, where a fall costs a climb; the portal caps that cost for the tape.
Remake runs are 10:00 rather than 2:00 because the THPS4 maps are large: LP34 cleared every College goal with about 5 minutes left (1:12:30), and the tape took ≈ 18 s of that from the street.
Letters in the remake are rearranged around new props (shipping containers, the purple statue, the mascot QP) but keep the original logic of a street half and a campus half (PS34).
remakeChanges: Tape: none in the 2002 PS2 career; PS1 hid one on a wire from the white building's top; the remake puts it on the clock-tower wire reached through the tower portal (LP34 1:10:00-1:10:04).
Timer: original free roam with per-goal clocks; remake 10:00 runs (LP34 1:07:10).

S stays on the Woodland School front (both); K moves from a power line reached from the garage gate (original) to a bunting wire from car-park deck 2 (remake); A moves from the garbage truck spine to shipping containers with a QP; T moves from the Fine Arts QP to a blue QP by a new purple statue; E moves from the Engineering handrail corner to an upper level reached by spine transfer from a mascot QP (G4m p003 vs PS34).
Officer Tom becomes Officer Dick; the banner goal is the same 7-banner wall grind (G4m p011 vs PS34).
The amateur C-O-M-B-O by the bridge becomes a pro goal in the remake with a similar bridge-side rail start (G4m p004 vs PS34).
Spine transfer over the wall becomes "Boneless Spine Transfer Between the Courts" (G4m p008 vs PS34).
Remake adds stat points, cash, a hidden deck, an Iron Galaxy logo (second wire from the tape-wire rooftop) and a panda plushie, several of them on the rooftop wire layer (PS34).
transfer: Landmark-wire crystal: build the level's tallest tower visible down the main axis, run a long descending rope or rail from its top to a lower roof, and put the crystal two-thirds of the way down. Access by a portal door at the back of the tower base (fast) or by grinding up from the roof end with tricks to hold speed (skilled). Our grind snap radius (2.1 m) and grind-ollie pop (≈ 2.4 m) make a ≈ 1-2 m drop from the door exit to the rail forgiving.

Gate-arm launch: place a sloped object (gate arm, ramp plank) under an overhead cable so a rail grind up the slope feeds a grind ollie (≈ 2.4 m above the rail) onto the cable; a letter or crystal shard on the cable teaches the wire layer early.
Teach then test: put an early collectible on a single cable 4-5 m up, a mid-level one on a roof-to-roof cable, and the crystal on the highest cable; each needs the previous lesson.

Rooftop chain alternative: wallride a boundary wall (wallie off it) into a bunting rope, hop to a second rope, then a roof; with no wallplant in our game, use wallride + wallie and a kicker at the wall base.
Flythrough tease: show the crystal in the level-intro camera beside a distinctive roof corner so players know where to look, then hide only the entrance (back door), not the crystal.

Permeable building: an open window on an upper storey reachable from a bowl kicker (PS1 Central Hall) gives a secret room with its own exit cable; good for an on-foot double jump (≈ 4.6 m) alternative if the board launch fails.
openQuestions: Exact remake tape position along the tower wire (LP34 registers it ≈ 2-3 s after launch, close to the brick building end, but WEB gamerant describes a long uphill grind from the roof to reach it).
Original PS2 tower portal: THG lists "Clock tower Grind" but no source describes the PS2 entrance; CC1 describes the portal for the PS1 port.

One web search summary claimed the remake tower door unlocks only after specific challenges; LP34 used it in the first run and PS34 lists no prerequisite. Unverified; the claimed source (ofzenandcomputing) refused the request.
Footprint scale depends on the G4m tennis courts being regulation size; no in-level reference with known size was measured.
Points for the PS2 gaps are not in the permitted sources.
PS1 tape access: how a player first reaches the top of the white building is not described in CC1.
